source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the optimal-treatment-strategy value and gives a necessary-and-sufficient pathwise-differentiability characterization; the categorical identification display here is its routine exchangeability/positivity specialization.

The public record is titled “Inference on Optimal Policy Values and Other Irregular Functionals via Smoothing” and lists Justin Whitehouse, Morgane Austern, and Vasilis Syrgkanis; its abstract describes a softmax-smoothing estimator and root-n convergence.

HAVER studies estimating the largest mean from samples of K distributions, proposes head averaging, and analyzes MSE; the inspected record does not state the grouped causal full-class all-estimator minimax theorem proposed here.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 61(5), 2015, pp. 2835–2885
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper is a minimax functional-estimation paper for discrete distributions and uses smooth/nonsmooth methodology, rather than a multivariate conditional ratio-maximum causal frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 62(6), 2016, pp. 3702–3720
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work derives entropy rates using best polynomial approximation and moment-matched priors, including a consistency threshold; it is an entropy result rather than the proposed K-variate maximum experiment.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 39(2), 2011, pp. 1012–1041
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats the Gaussian ℓ1 norm using composite fuzzy hypotheses, chi-square control, polynomial approximation, and Hermite lifts, providing a methodological template rather than this causal maximum result.
The preprint proves an Omega(sqrt(K)) approximate-degree lower bound for Boolean OR; the stated 1/14 formulation is consistent with Theorem 7.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(522), 2018, pp. 780–788
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops parametric-rate inference for maxima of indexed parameters, including growing-index discussion, under remainder and regularity conditions rather than sparse-table all-regime minimax risk.

The paper concerns observational offline multi-action policy learning with augmented inverse-propensity weighting and asymptotically minimax-optimal regret over restricted policy classes, not oracle-value MSE.
